fixed.explanation: filterCookies prepended '.' to host-only domains, so they matched subdomains. It also used a plain startsWith on the path, so a /api cookie matched /apiv2. The fix matches host-only cookies by exact hostname and applies the RFC 6265 path-match rule: the paths are equal, or the cookie path is a prefix that ends in '/', or the next character in the request path is '/'. pathMatches appended '/' to both sides, so a /foo/ cookie matched /foo. It now uses the same rule, so /foo/ no longer matches /foo.

query.intent: Cookie filtering by URL in the browser context cookie store: the domain match, path match, and secure checks used when returning cookies for URLs or when deciding which cookies to send. Domain matching must treat host-only cookies as exact host matches, and path matching must follow RFC 6265 path-match rules (prefix must end at a '/' boundary).
query.symptom: Cookie URL matching is wrong: host-only cookies are returned for subdomains, a /api cookie matches /apiv2, and a /foo/ cookie is sent to /foo.

history.analysis: filterCookies in network.ts does the URL filtering for listing cookies. It adds a leading '.' to host-only domains, so they match subdomains. It also uses a plain startsWith on the path, so a /api cookie matches /apiv2. pathMatches in cookieStore.ts appends '/' to both sides, so a /foo/ cookie matches /foo. domainMatches already handles host-only cookies correctly.
